title: The IBM Music Card ports and OPP registers
covers: the sixteen ports of the IBM Music Feature Card at its base address, and the register file of the Yamaha OPP that its Z80 drives

searched.gave: The header of imfc.cpp credits Loris Chiocca's reverse engineering of the card's Z80 ROM and the Virtual FB-01 project, and cites no Yamaha document.
IBM's PC Music Feature Technical Reference (March 1987) documents the card's ports and voice parameters, never the OPP's register numbers.
The Yamaha components listing holds no YM2164 or OPP document.
The IBM PC Music Feature Technical Reference is there; no YM2164 datasheet.
Datasheet indexes name no YM2164 datasheet; the YM2151 manual describes a different part.

rows.text: Port 0 (PIU0) is at base address +0 and its bits 0-7 carry data bits 0-7 of the card's 9-bit word.
Reading PIU0 clears RxRDY, which is why bit 8 is read from PIU2 before the byte.
Base port +0 is installed as readPortPIU0 for a read and writePortPIU0 for a write.
The read returns port 0's stored value and, in mode 1 as an input, marks the byte acknowledged; no RxRDY flag of PIU2 is cleared.
A write stores the byte into port 0 only while port 0 is an output; otherwise it logs and drops it.
Port 1 (PIU1) is at base address +1, sends data from the system to the card, and its bits 0-7 are data bits 0-7.
Writing PIU1 clears TxRDY.
Base port +1 is installed as readPortPIU1 and writePortPIU1.
A write stores the byte into port 1 and, in mode 1 as an output, marks data available; no TxRDY flag is cleared.
A write to port 1 while it is an input is logged and dropped.
A read returns the stored output byte and, in mode 1 as an input, also acknowledges the data.
PIU2 is a read and write register at base address +2.
Bits 2 and 4 are the TxRDY and RxRDY interrupt enables, set only through the PCR's bit set/reset command.
Base port +2 is installed as readPortPIU2 and writePortPIU2.
A write sets port 2's pins directly while their group is in mode 0, bits 2 and 4 included, so the PCR is not the only way they change.
A read returns port 2's pins; bit 2 takes group 1's two enables in mode 1, bit 4 the same two under group 0's mode 1 input.
The two enables the read reports are internal flags written by clearing the port and by the control register's bit 2 command.
The PIU is initialized by writing [BC] to the PCR.
The register at base address +3 initializes the PIU and performs bit set/reset of PIU2.
The commands are [BC] to initialize, [05] and [04] to set and reset bit 2, and [09] and [08] to set and reset bit 4.
Base port +3 is installed as readPortPCR and writePortPCR.
A write with bit 7 set selects both groups' modes and directions, logs them, then clears every port's bits.
With bit 7 clear, pins 2 and 4 set and reset their interrupt enables as documented, and pin 6 sets the group 0 write enable.
In mode 0 the same command writes the selected pin directly while its port is an output, and logs a warning otherwise.
A read of the control register returns 0.
CNTRO at base address +4 carries timer A's count data and feeds bit 0 of the Total Status Register and the jumper's IRQ level.
The document asks that counter 0 be used in 8253 mode 2; the countdown resolution is two microseconds and the setting range 2 through 65535.
Reading base address +4 returns count data for timer A.
Writing base address +4 sets timer A's count, from 2 through 65535.
Base port +4 is installed as readPortCNTR0 and writePortCNTR0.
The first byte written becomes the high half and the second the low half of a 16-bit count, which accepts 0 and 1 too.
A read without a latch command returns 0; after one it returns the latched low byte and then the high byte.
The counter's byte is read through readCounterByte.
CNTR1 at base address +5 carries timer B's count data and feeds bit 1 of the Total Status Register and the jumper's IRQ level.
The document asks that counter 1 be used in mode 2, with counter 2 as its prescaler; the resolution is their product times 0.5 microseconds, the range 2 through 65535.
Reading base address +5 returns count data for timer B.
Writing base address +5 sets timer B's count, from 2 through 65535.
Base port +5 is installed as readPortCNTR1 and writePortCNTR1.
The first byte written becomes the high half and the second the low half of a 16-bit count; no range is enforced.
A read returns 0 unless a latch command was issued, then the latched low byte and next the high byte.
The counter's byte is read through readCounterByte.
CNTR2 at base address +6 holds timer B's prescaler data and drives counter 1.
Reading base address +6 returns the prescaler data for timer B.
Writing base address +6 sets the prescaler, from 2 through 65535.
Base port +6 is installed as readPortCNTR2 and writePortCNTR2.
The first byte written becomes the high half and the second the low half of a 16-bit prescaler; no range is enforced.
A read returns 0 unless a latch command was issued, then the latched low byte and next the high byte.
The counter's byte is read through readCounterByte.
The card's PIT is software-compatible with the 8253: counter 0 is timer A and counters 1 and 2 together are timer B.
TCWR at base address +7 sets each counter's operating mode and latches its current count.
The mode words are [34], [74] and [B6], and the latch commands are [00], [40] and [80].
Base port +7 is installed as readPortTCWR and writePortTCWR.
A write outside those six values is logged as unsupported and stores nothing.
A read of the control register returns 0.
After a latch command, a 16-bit read returns the low byte and then the high byte.
Without a latch the read returns 0 twice and returns to the live path.
Only counter 0's output falls and rises with time; a TODO marks the other timers as not done.
The Total Control Register is at base address +8, and +9 through +B show an image of it.
Bit 0 is stored as timer A's interrupt clear, usually 1; a 0 clears the interrupt and the bit is immediately reset to 1.
Bit 1 is stored as timer B's interrupt clear, usually 1; a 0 clears the interrupt and the bit is immediately reset to 1.
Bit 2 stores the interrupt-enable flag for timer A.
Bit 3 stores the interrupt-enable flag for timer B.
Bit 4 stores the eighth data bit the system sends with PIU1.
Bit 6 stores the total IRQ mask: 0 masks every interrupt request the card generates, 1 does not.
Bit 7 stores the IRQ bus enable, which connects or floats the card's IRQ lines on the system bus; the document asks it be set before TMSK.
To handle overlapping requests a routine masks all sources, polls them, resets their bits, issues EOI and unmasks.
Ports +8 through +B are installed in a loop as readPortTCR and writePortTCR.
Base address +8 holds the eight bits listed: IRQ enable, total IRQ mask, the transmit data bit, two timer enables and two timer clears; bit 5 is not used.
The Total Status Register is at base address +C, and +D through +F show an image of it.
Bit 0 reports timer A's IRQ status: 1 while timer A generates an interrupt, cleared with it.
Bit 1 reports timer B's IRQ status: 1 while timer B generates an interrupt, cleared with it.
Bit 7 reports the card's total IRQ: 1 when timer A, timer B, TxRDY or RxRDY generates one.
Ports +C through +F are installed in a loop as readPortTSR and writePortTSR.
Base address +C reports bits 0, 1 and 7.
A write to the status register changes nothing.
The value's eight bits become timer A's index bits 9-2 and the index's two low bits stay.
A write stores that high byte into timer A's index.
The card's Z80 writes it through register_w and data_w of the OPP.
The value's two low bits become timer A's index bits 1-0 and the upper bits stay.
A write stores that low part into timer A's index.
The card's Z80 writes it through register_w and data_w of the OPP.
The whole value becomes timer B's time index.
A write stores the index of timer B.
The card's Z80 writes it through register_w and data_w of the OPP.
The value is stored as the timer enables and CSM mode; the code that would reset flags or start and stop the timers is commented out.
A write stores the enable byte and starts no timer.
The card's Z80 writes it through register_w and data_w of the OPP.
The high nibble scales the LFO's overflow count and the low nibble sets its increment.
A write stores both LFO frequency halves.
The card's Z80 writes it through register_w and data_w of the OPP.
With bit 7 set the low seven bits are stored as PMD, otherwise as AMD.
A write stores the depth in one of the two LFO depth fields.
The card's Z80 writes it through register_w and data_w of the OPP.
Bits 7-6 are stored as the clock test value and bits 1-0 as the LFO waveform.
A write stores the clock test and the waveform.
The card's Z80 writes it through register_w and data_w of the OPP.
Bit 6 sets pan[channel*2], bit 7 sets pan[channel*2+1], bits 5-3 the feedback shift and bits 2-0 the connection.
A write stores feedback, the two outputs and the connection, then rebuilds that channel's algorithm.
The card's Z80 writes it through register_w and data_w of the OPP.
The value's low seven bits are stored as the channel's key code, copied to its four operators with their frequencies recomputed.
A write stores the key code and recomputes the four operators' frequency and detune.
The card's Z80 writes it through register_w and data_w of the OPP.
The value's upper six bits are stored as the key fraction inside the channel's frequency index.
A write stores the key fraction and recomputes the four operators' frequencies.
The card's Z80 writes it through register_w and data_w of the OPP.
Bits 6-4 are stored as the phase modulation sensitivity and bits 1-0 as the amplitude one.
A write stores the two modulation sensitivities.
The card's Z80 writes it through register_w and data_w of the OPP.
Bits 6-4 are stored as the detune and bits 3-0 as the frequency multiple, and the operator's frequency follows.
A write stores detune and multiple, and recomputes the operator's frequency and detune.
The card's Z80 writes it through register_w and data_w of the OPP.
Bits 6-0 are stored as the operator's total level, shifted left three bits onto the ten-bit envelope scale.
A write stores the seven low bits as the total level of the operator the register addresses.
The card's Z80 ROM routine, ported into the host, writes it through register_w and data_w of the YM2151 device, one call for the number and one for the value.
Bits 7-6 store the key scale as five minus their value, and bits 4-0 the attack rate as twice their value plus 32, or zero.
A write stores key scale and attack rate, recomputes the attack rate's table entry when either changed, and the other three rates' when the key scale changed.
The attack rate's table index is the attack rate plus the key code shifted right by the key scale.
The card's Z80 ROM routine, ported into the host, writes it through register_w and data_w of the YM2151 device, one call for the number and one for the value.
Bit 7 enables amplitude modulation by the LFO, and bits 4-0 store the first decay rate as twice their value plus 32, or zero.
A write stores the AM mask and the first decay rate, then recomputes that rate's table entry.
The first decay rate's table index is the rate plus the key code shifted right by the key scale.
The card's Z80 ROM routine, ported into the host, writes it through register_w and data_w of the YM2151 device, one call for the number and one for the value.
Bits 7-6 index a four-entry table of second detune values, 0, 384, 500 and 608; bits 4-0 store the second decay rate as twice their value plus 32, or zero.
A write stores the detune and second decay rate, recomputes the operator's frequency when the detune changed, and the rate's table entry.
The second decay rate's table index is the rate plus the key code shifted right by the key scale.
The card's Z80 ROM routine, ported into the host, writes it through register_w and data_w of the YM2151 device, one call for the number and one for the value.
Bits 7-4 index a table into the operator's first decay level, and bits 3-0 store the release rate as four times their value plus 34.
A write stores the first decay level and release rate, then recomputes the release rate's table entry.
The release rate's table index is the rate plus the key code shifted right by the key scale.
The card's Z80 ROM routine, ported into the host, writes it through register_w and data_w of the YM2151 device, one call for the number and one for the value.
